title: Washington's 1793 proclamation says the United States will be friendly and impartial toward the belligerents
summary: Washington's 1793 proclamation declares a friendly and impartial conduct toward the European belligerents.
body: Washington's proclamation of 22 April 1793 says the United States will adopt a conduct friendly and impartial toward the belligerent powers. The proclamation is a policy in the wars of the French Revolution. It is not the later farewell address. The wording on the page includes: "require, that they should with sincerity and good faith adopt and pursue a conduct friendly and impartial toward the belligerant Powers; I have therefore thought fit by these presents to declare the disposition of the United States to observe the conduct aforesaid towards those Powers respectfully; and to exhort and warn the citizens of the United States carefully to avoid all acts and".
